newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING Barings confirms OTP "LT buy" rating.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings confirms OTP "LT buy" rating.

text.p: London-based security house ING Barings maintained its "Long-term buy" rating for Hungary's largest commercial bank, OTP, in a company update on Friday.
"OTP has reported unconsolidated net profit of HUF4.8bln for 1H96, in line with our profit forecast of HUF9.4bln for the full year," ING Barings said.

A cooler economy and changed accounting rules caused OTP's net interest income to increase by only 14.9 percent in the first half of this year to 28.1 billion forints from the same period of last year, ING said.
However, adjusted for changes in the accounting treatment for non-accrued interest, net interest income rose 25.9 percent, it added.
A strict and effective cost control programme, higher net fee income and better asset quality improved the bank's operating profit significantly, ING said.

OTP's non-consolidated assets amounted to 1,129.6 billion forints on June 30, which meant a 10 percent drop in real terms. Commercial, retail loans and loans to municipalities declined, but loans to companies rose, with the share of small businesses dropping, ING said.

As a result of a slight improvement in asset quality, provisions in the balance sheet for non-performing loans had fallen to 28 billion forints by June 30 from 30.7 billion at the end of June 1995, it said.

"We believe that even if investors are cautious about the relatively low level of loan loss provisions (HUF 2.6bln versus our full year forecast of HUF 9bln) significant growth in fee income and effective wage controls should provide some reassurance that OTP is likely to achieve our profit forecast," it added.

The number of current accounts, OTP's main line of busienss, grew to 1.4 million in the first half of this year from 1.3 million. Although its market share continued to shrink, OTP retained its leading position in municipal lending and improved its share of corporate business, ING said.
